newsitem.title: USA: N.J. approves South Jersey Gas program.
newsitem.headline: N.J. approves South Jersey Gas program.

text.p: New Jersey, in another step toward a deregulated natural gas market, approved South Jersey Gas Co's proposal to give 10,000 customers a choice of gas supplier, the state's Board of Public Utilities said Monday.

"The board's approval of this program will begin to give residents in south Jersey a true choice in selecting the natural gas supplier of their choice. We expect competition in this market to lead to lower rates and to a new range of services and pricing options," Herbert Tate, Board of Public Utilities president, said in a statement.
The pilot program, set to begin in April, will offer supplier choice to 10,000 out of 228,000 South Jersey Gas residential customers on a first come, first served basis.
The program will run until June 30, 1998, or later if approved by the Board, and contains significant consumer safeguards.
The utility will continue to deliver the natural gas through its existing distribution system and will continue to offer customer services such as meter checking and appliance maintenance and repair.
South Jersey Gas serves customers in Atlantic, Burlington, Camden, Cape May, Cumberland, Gloucester and Salem counties.
The residential program follows successful introduction in 1994 of retail competition to the company's commercial and industrial customers.
New Jersey was the first state to introduce retail competition to all commercial and industrial customers of the state's four natural gas utilities.
Last week, the board approved New Jersey Natural Gas Co's pilot proposal that will give up to 30,000 of its 335,000 residential customers the opportunity to choose their natural gas supplier.
